stem: Kim is a 10-year-old girl with asthma. At camp, she used her counsellor’s orange puffer twice a day because her own puffer fell into the swimming pool on the first day. Her parents ask what they should know about the counsellor’s orange puffer. What can you tell them?

options.text: The colour of the puffer indicates the manufacturer but all manufacturers make the same medication
The colour of the puffer indicates the type of generic medication but all generic medications are the same strength
The colour of the puffer indicates the strength of the medication but all orange puffers are the same strength
The colour of the puffer indicates the manufacturer and type of generic medication but not all orange puffers are the same strength

explanation: In asthma inhalers, colour alone does not reliably identify the medication or its strength. Different manufacturers may use similar colours for different formulations, so inhalers should always be checked by the name and dose, not colour.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: This tests recognition that inhaler colours are not interchangeable and medication should be identified by name and dose.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: the colour does not simply indicate manufacturer, and different manufacturers do not all make the same medication.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: colour does not define a generic medication type, and generic products are not all the same strength.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: colour does not reliably indicate strength, and orange puffers are not all equivalent.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: inhaler colour can relate to branding or product presentation, but it does not guarantee the same medication or strength.
